recipe.name: Slow-Baked Broccoli Frittata
recipe.description: A thick, custardy frittata packed with pan-roasted broccoli and red onion, baked low and slow. A squeeze of lemon, olive oil and grated cheese finish it off.

ingredients.ingredient_name: Grated Parmigiano Reggiano, for the eggs
Extra-virgin olive oil, for the broccoli
Extra-virgin olive oil, for the onion
Extra-virgin olive oil, for the garlic

steps: Set the oven to 400°F (200°C) to preheat.
Whisk the eggs with the Parmigiano Reggiano, salt and black pepper in a large bowl, then set aside.
Trim 1/2 inch (1 cm) from the broccoli stem. Cut off the florets with their stalks attached, then halve them, quartering large ones so all are even.
Heat the olive oil over medium-high heat in an ovenproof sauté pan about 10–11 inches (25–28 cm) wide.
Add the broccoli and leave it mostly undisturbed until deep brown on one side. Flip the pieces and add a pinch of salt.
Roast the pan of broccoli in the oven for 10–15 minutes, until tender.
Heat more olive oil in a second sauté pan of the same size over medium-high heat while the broccoli roasts.
Add the red onion and a pinch of salt. Cook for 3–5 minutes, stirring sometimes, until lightly browned.
Return the broccoli pan to the stove over medium heat, using an oven mitt for the hot handle. Turn the oven down to 300°F (150°C).
Rewarm the broccoli, then stir in the garlic, pepper flakes and a little more olive oil for 1 minute, without letting the garlic colour.
Stir the cooked onion into the broccoli until evenly mixed.
Pour in the egg mixture and raise the heat to high for 30 seconds.
Bake at 300°F (150°C) for 25–30 minutes, until the egg is only just set.
Loosen the frittata with a rubber spatula and, using an oven mitt on the hot handle, turn it out onto a serving plate.
Finish with a squeeze of lemon juice, a thin drizzle of olive oil and a sprinkle of Parmigiano Reggiano.
You nailed it! Grab a plate and dig in.
